newsitem.title: UK: Russian aid money stolen at London airport.
newsitem.headline: Russian aid money stolen at London airport.

text.p: About $2.5 million of American aid destined for Russia has been stolen from London's Heathrow airport, police said on Sunday.
The money was stolen from a high-security cargo compound while awaiting transfer from a New York flight to a plane bound for Moscow.
The cash was in one of four bags, containing a total of $10 million, that were being transferred from a strongroom for loading into a sealed container.
Security officers raised the alarm after noticing that the seals on the container were broken.
All cargo and security staff have been interviewed but no arrests have been made.

The Mail on Sunday said the money, in high denomination dollar bills, came from the Republic National Bank of New York and was being sent to the Moscow-based Toko Bank as part of U.S. aid funding for the Russian economy.
British Airways has launched a review of how valuable cargo transfers are handled at the airport.
